content.text: A 1500-calorie daily intake creates a moderate calorie deficit for most adults while still providing sufficient protein, healthy fats, and carbohydrates to fuel daily activities and preserve muscle mass.
Do not drop below 1,200 calories (women) or 1,500 calories (men) without medical supervision. Severe restriction slows metabolism and leads to muscle loss.

Breakfast: Greek yogurt (150g) + berries + 1 tbsp honey = 220 cal. Snack: 1 medium apple + 15g almonds = 150 cal. Lunch: Chicken & veggie rice bowl = 480 cal. Snack: Protein shake = 180 cal. Dinner: Baked cod with sweet potato and green beans = 465 cal.

items.question: Is 1500 calories too low?
items.answer: For most women, 1500 calories creates a healthy 300–500 calorie deficit. For men, this may be too low. Use a TDEE calculator to find your personal calorie target before following any plan.

items.question: How fast will I lose weight on 1500 calories?
items.answer: Most people lose 0.5–1 lb (0.2–0.45 kg) per week on a 500-calorie daily deficit, which is the healthiest and most sustainable rate of weight loss.
